citation: Frances Benjamin Johnston, '[Horse and groom in a field at Tuskegee Normal and Industrial Institute, Alabama]', glass negative, ca. 1902. Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division, Frances Benjamin Johnston Collection, LC-J694- 151, LC-DIG-ds-17290 (item 2024631576).
author: Frances Benjamin Johnston
repository: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division. Reference image 17290v.jpg (1024 x 819) of the digital file from the original cyanotype, read at tile.loc.gov; a crop of the groom is kept in kevinrhaas/chicago-evidence evidence/people-references-2026-11-07/stable_helper_1904/.
locator: The whole frame: a dark horse in a halter standing broadside in a ploughed field, a young groom at its head on the right of the picture, holding the lead rope, seen full length from his left front at about eight metres.
rights_note: LOC rights advisory: 'No known restrictions on publication.' Used only as a reference picture for a stable hand's working dress (T-3484); nothing is traced or sampled from it.
access_notes: Viewed 2026-11-07 (T-3484). The catalogue's date (ca. 1902) is from the negative's caption card. The groom works in his shirt sleeves: a pale shirt with fine dark stripes, long sleeves buttoned at the wrist, a tall white standing collar closed at the throat, no coat and no waistcoat; dark braces over the shoulders; a belt at the waist of dark straight trousers worn long over his shoes; a light felt hat with a creased crown and a short brim. He holds the halter rope short in his right hand and its loop in his left. Not Chicago and not of any named man; the role and decade are the 1904 scene's.
note: One of the 1904 stable helper's reference pictures (data/people_match/reference_sets/stable_helper_1904.json).
what_it_supplies: a groom's working dress about 1902, worn at work with a horse: striped shirt in shirt sleeves, collar, braces, belt, dark trousers, light felt hat
how the shirt's sleeves and the braces read on a working man full length at street distance
what_it_does_not_supply: colour (a monochrome print): the stripe's colour and the trousers' cloth are not given
anything about Chicago, the Glessner stable or August Billings; no likeness is asserted
